cards.title: Egypt vs IR Iran
cards.headline: Egypt Appears to Have Won — Market Hasn't Caught Up
cards.summary: Multiple post-match sources indicate Egypt defeated Iran in their World Cup group stage match, yet the market still prices Egypt at just 39.5%, suggesting severe lag behind the actual result.
why: Several independent post-match discussions celebrate Egypt's win with full-time stats (66% possession, 9 shots)
Match kicked off at 11 PM ET on June 26 and appears to have concluded with an Egypt victory
Market pricing at 39.5% implies massive mispricing if the result is confirmed
cards.watch_item: Official FIFA or tournament confirmation of the final score — one source hints at a possible draw scenario ('both get 4 points') which would invalidate the Egypt win call

cards.title: Golden Glove Winner
cards.headline: Vozinha Massively Overpriced for Golden Glove at 47%
cards.summary: Cape Verde's goalkeeper Vozinha is trading at 47% for the World Cup Golden Glove despite the award historically going to keepers from semifinalist or finalist nations — a threshold Cape Verde is extremely unlikely to reach.
why: Golden Glove has gone to keepers from champion or finalist nations in 4 of the last 5 World Cups
Cape Verde's heroic group-stage draws created narrative hype but the team is unlikely to advance deep into knockouts
The expanded 48-team format means deep-run keepers will play 6-7 matches, diluting early-round saves
cards.watch_item: If Cape Verde pulls off knockout upsets and reaches the quarterfinals or beyond, the narrative premium becomes justified

cards.title: Portugal vs. Uzbekistan: O/U 2.5
cards.headline: Portugal 5-0 Uzbekistan: Over 2.5 Goals Easily Cleared
cards.summary: The match is final with Portugal thrashing Uzbekistan 5-0, decisively clearing the Over 2.5 goals threshold. The market price of 65.5% appears stale and does not reflect the confirmed outcome.
why: Final score confirmed at 5-0, nearly double the 2.5-goal threshold
Match is complete with multiple credible sources confirming the result
Ronaldo scored twice in a historic performance, contributing to a dominant win
cards.watch_item: Whether the market is still open and tradeable at the displayed price, or has already frozen/resolved

cards.title: Tunisia vs Japan
cards.headline: Japan Already Won 4-0 — Market Still Priced at 67.5%
cards.summary: Japan defeated Tunisia 4-0 in a match confirmed as complete by multiple major outlets, yet the market still shows Japan at only 67.5% probability — a massive mispricing on a settled outcome.
why: Japan beat Tunisia 4-0; the match is over and the result is confirmed
Market price of 67.5% implies uncertainty where none exists — fair value is 100%
Over 32 cents of edge per contract if orders can be filled before settlement
cards.watch_item: Whether displayed prices are actually fillable — liquidity on stale post-match markets often evaporates before orders execute

cards.title: Paraguay vs Australia
cards.headline: World Cup Draw Massively Overpriced: Sell Tie in Paraguay vs Australia
cards.summary: Kalshi prices a draw at 43.5% for this World Cup Group D finale, but sportsbook consensus puts the fair value around 28-32% — a glaring 11.5-point mispricing even after accounting for a potential collusion premium.
why: Major sportsbooks have Paraguay as the clear favorite (~43% implied), not a coin flip with a draw
Kalshi's 43.5% draw price is 15+ points above the vig-removed sportsbook consensus of ~28%
Both teams need results on 3 points each, reducing incentive to play for a passive draw
cards.watch_item: If both teams discover mid-match that a draw guarantees mutual advancement (based on the simultaneous USA-Türkiye result), tactical collusion could push the true draw probability higher than estimated

cards.title: France vs Iraq
cards.headline: France Already Won 3-0 — Market Still Hasn't Settled
cards.summary: France defeated Iraq 3-0 in their World Cup match on June 22, confirmed by all major sports outlets. The market is still trading France at 89.5¢ despite the result being final, creating a risk-free arbitrage opportunity.
why: Final score confirmed: France 3, Iraq 0 — match is over
France contract pays $1.00 but is priced at only 89.5¢ due to settlement lag
Tie and Iraq contracts are worthless but still trading above zero
cards.watch_item: Platform settlement timing — once the market officially resolves, the arbitrage window closes

cards.title: Spain vs Argentina: Goalscorer
cards.headline: Lautaro Martinez Overpriced at 19% to Score in World Cup Final
cards.summary: Lautaro Martinez has been a substitute all tournament and faces the best defense in the competition, making his 19% market price significantly inflated versus a fair value around 11%.
why: Martinez is expected to play only ~25 minutes as a late substitute
Spain has conceded just 1 goal in 7 tournament games — the best defensive record
Limited minutes against an elite defense makes scoring highly unlikely
cards.watch_item: Argentina falling behind early or a tactical shift that sees Martinez start, which would dramatically increase his minutes and scoring probability

cards.title: 2026 FIFA World Cup Winner
cards.headline: Spain Underpriced as World Cup Enters Knockout Rounds
cards.summary: With the Round of 16 underway, Spain at 12.65% is modestly underpriced relative to a ~15% fair value, while France at 34.65% appears significantly overpriced given the structural difficulty of winning three more knockout matches.
why: Spain's Euro championship pedigree and elite squad depth support a higher fair probability than the market reflects
France needs three consecutive knockout wins including a dangerous Morocco quarterfinal — the market underestimates this difficulty
Host-nation sentiment is inflating prices for Norway, Mexico, and USA, creating selling opportunities
cards.watch_item: Spain faces Portugal in the Round of 16 — an immediate elimination would invalidate the thesis entirely

cards.title: Mexico vs England
cards.headline: England Underpriced to Advance Past Mexico in World Cup Knockout Match
cards.summary: With the match at 0-0, England's odds to advance are trading at 48.5% on Kalshi versus 55-58% implied by major sportsbooks — a significant gap likely driven by home-crowd and nationalist retail bias on the platform.
why: Sportsbook consensus prices England at 55-58% to advance, creating a 6-9% edge over Kalshi's current line
Kalshi's US-based retail audience likely inflating Mexico due to proximity bias and home-crowd sentiment
England's superior squad depth and tournament form (Kane with 5 goals) supports higher advancement probability
cards.watch_item: A Mexico goal would instantly validate current Kalshi pricing and eliminate the edge — this is a live match where dynamics can shift in seconds

cards.title: USA vs Belgium
cards.headline: USA Underpriced to Advance Past Belgium in World Cup Knockout Round
cards.summary: The market prices USA's advancement at 52.5%, but sportsbook consensus and key match factors point to a fair probability closer to 57%, creating a modest but real edge worth backing.
why: Sportsbook consensus prices USA to advance at 55-58%, well above the current 52.5% market price
Home advantage in Seattle boosts USA in extra time/penalties scenarios, plus Balogun returns from suspension
Belgium's shaky form—needing an 86th-minute comeback vs Senegal—contrasts with USA's 3-win momentum
cards.watch_item: Belgium's 90-minute moneyline shows them as slight regulation favorites; if pre-match odds shift further toward Belgium or a key USA injury emerges, the edge could evaporate

cards.title: Jordan vs Argentina
cards.headline: Argentina Overpriced in Dead-Rubber World Cup Match vs Jordan
cards.summary: With Argentina already clinching Group J and Messi confirmed benched, the market's 84.5% win probability is inflated by roughly 4-5 percentage points compared to a fair value near 80%.
why: Messi confirmed benched and heavy squad rotation expected in a meaningless group-stage closer
Argentina has zero competitive incentive—Group J already clinched
Sportsbook consensus (adjusted for vig) places Argentina around 80-82%, not 84.5%
cards.watch_item: Any indication Scaloni deploys a stronger-than-expected lineup or brings Messi on early as a substitute

cards.title: Cape Verde vs Saudi Arabia
cards.headline: Cape Verde vs Saudi Arabia: Draw Looks Underpriced in Group H Decider
cards.summary: The draw at 28.5% appears undervalued by roughly 4-5 percentage points given Cape Verde's proven defensive resilience and Saudi Arabia's poor recent form, creating actionable value on the tie outcome.
why: Cape Verde unbeaten in group play (drew Spain 0-0, Uruguay 2-2), showing elite defensive and counterattacking ability
Saudi Arabia's 4-0 demolition by Spain exposes a major quality gap vs Cape Verde's results against the same opponents
Must-win pressure on Saudi Arabia historically doesn't convert to actual wins, while Cape Verde may only need a draw to advance
cards.watch_item: If the Spain-Uruguay result changes Cape Verde's advancement math, they may push for a win rather than play for the draw, reducing tie probability

cards.title: Curacao vs Ivory Coast
cards.headline: Curacao Draw Underpriced Against Must-Win Ivory Coast
cards.summary: The draw outcome at 10.5% is underpriced by roughly 4-5 percentage points given Curacao's proven defensive resilience and the tactical dynamics of facing a desperate Ivory Coast side.
why: Curacao held Ecuador to 0-0 with 15 saves, proving elite defensive capability under pressure
Ivory Coast's must-win desperation creates all-out attacking that paradoxically opens space for defensive counterstrategies
Sportsbook consensus for draws in this matchup range clusters around 15-18%, well above the current 10.5% price
cards.watch_item: Early Ivory Coast goal would kill draw probability — monitor pre-match lineup and tactical setup for signs of Curacao's defensive commitment vs. a potential collapse like their 7-1 loss to Germany

cards.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina vs Qatar
cards.headline: Bosnia Overpriced at 71.5% — Sell Against Sharp Consensus
cards.summary: Bosnia and Herzegovina's win probability is trading above sportsbook-implied fair value (~67%), with their historically draw-heavy record against Qatar and both teams' desperation further compressing the edge.
why: Sportsbook consensus (Pinnacle, DraftKings) implies Bosnia at ~68-70%, below Kalshi's 71.5%
Head-to-head record shows 4 draws in 5 meetings — Bosnia has never beaten Qatar
Both teams in must-win situations, which historically elevates draw probability
cards.watch_item: Pre-match line movement — if sharp sportsbooks shift toward Bosnia before kickoff, the edge narrows or disappears

cards.title: Colombia vs Portugal
cards.headline: Portugal Overpriced at 48.5% for Group K Finale vs Colombia
cards.summary: Portugal's win probability is priced at 48.5% on Kalshi but sportsbook-implied odds suggest a fair value closer to 43-45%, creating a modest sell opportunity on Portugal.
why: Sportsbook odds imply Portugal's true win probability is 3-5 points lower than the current market price
Both teams are likely already qualified, raising the chance Portugal rotates key players
Colombia's excellent recent form (including 3-1 over Uzbekistan) makes them a live underdog
cards.watch_item: Colombia's result vs DR Congo on June 23 could reshape both teams' motivation and tactical approach for the final group match

cards.title: England vs Ghana
cards.headline: England Overpriced at 80.5% — Sell for ~4.5% Edge
cards.summary: Sportsbook consensus prices England's win probability at roughly 76%, making Kalshi's 80.5% line too rich. Selling England YES offers medium-confidence value given potential rotation and Ghana's defensive posture.
why: Sharp sportsbook lines cluster around 75-79% for England, well below Kalshi's 80.5%
England may rotate key attackers (Saka likely benched, Rashford injury concern) with qualification already in hand
Ghana's defensive setup after their 1-0 opener raises draw probability beyond what Kalshi implies
cards.watch_item: Any late team news confirming England fields a full-strength XI would narrow the edge and weaken the case for selling.

cards.title: South Africa vs Canada
cards.headline: South Africa vs Canada: Thin Edge Not Worth the Risk
cards.summary: Sportsbook odds suggest South Africa has roughly a 30% chance to advance past Canada in this Round of 32 knockout match, slightly higher than the market's 26.5% implied probability, but the 3.5-point edge is too thin to act on confidently.
why: Sportsbook moneylines imply Canada ~59% to win in 90 minutes, but knockout format (extra time + penalties) gives South Africa additional equity to ~30%
Market prices South Africa at 26.5% — a small 3.5-point gap from fair value that doesn't justify a bet against a clear favorite
Historical pattern: fading market favorites on sub-4-point edges in World Cup knockouts has not been profitable
cards.watch_item: Any lineup or injury news on game day that could meaningfully shift Canada's advantage or South Africa's defensive setup under coach Hugo Broos

cards.title: Croatia vs Ghana
cards.headline: Ghana Underpriced at 16.5% in Must-Win Scenario for Croatia
cards.summary: Ghana's market price of 16.5% to win appears roughly 3.5 percentage points below fair value (~20%), given their strong defensive record and favorable tactical position needing only a draw to advance from Group L.
why: Ghana has conceded 0 goals in 2 matches (including 0-0 vs England) and only needs a draw to top the group
Croatia must attack to win, creating tactical asymmetry that favors Ghana counter-attacks and draws
Sportsbook consensus implies Ghana's win probability is 18-22%, well above the current 16.5% market price
cards.watch_item: Any late team news or line movement suggesting Croatia's attack has found form—an early Croatian goal would collapse Ghana's sit-deep-and-counter strategy

cards.title: New Zealand vs Belgium
cards.headline: Belgium Overpriced at 82.5% Given World Cup Attacking Woes
cards.summary: Belgium's 82.5% win probability appears 3-4 percentage points too high given they've drawn both prior group-stage matches (1-1 vs Egypt, 0-0 vs Iran) and sharp sportsbooks price their fair value closer to 78-80%.
why: Belgium have failed to win either group match, drawing 100% of games despite superior talent
Sharp sportsbook fair value places Belgium at ~78-80%, making 82.5% overpriced
Historical draw rates for favorites in World Cup group stages are elevated, and the tie at 11.5% looks underpriced
cards.watch_item: An early Belgium goal would instantly validate or exceed the current market price and eliminate the edge

cards.title: Switzerland vs Canada
cards.headline: Canada Underpriced at Home in World Cup Group Decider
cards.summary: Canada's win probability appears undervalued at 29.5% for a high-stakes Group B finale at BC Place in Vancouver, with sportsbook consensus placing them closer to 31-33% after accounting for home advantage and recent form.
why: Home crowd advantage at BC Place in Vancouver should boost Canada's chances
Jonathan David in red-hot form with 3 goals, team coming off dominant 6-0 win
Sportsbook consensus prices Canada ~2-3 points higher than current market odds
cards.watch_item: Pre-match line movement—if Canada's odds drift further or key injury news (e.g., impact of losing midfielder Koné) shifts the consensus, the edge could evaporate

cards.title: Ecuador vs Germany
cards.headline: Ecuador Underpriced in Dead-Rubber Clash Against Already-Qualified Germany
cards.summary: Germany have already clinched Group E with a perfect record, creating strong incentives to rotate their squad ahead of the knockout round. Ecuador, desperate for a must-win result to stay alive, appear underpriced at 21.5% against a fair value closer to 25%.
why: Germany locked up the group (2-0, +7 GD) and have clear incentive to rest starters before the Round of 32
Ecuador must win to survive—maximum desperation against a potential B-team
Sportsbook consensus places Ecuador's win probability at ~25%, a meaningful gap above the current market price
cards.watch_item: Whether Germany manager Nagelsmann announces significant squad rotation or opts to keep his starting XI sharp for knockout play

cards.title: Senegal vs Iraq
cards.headline: Senegal vs Iraq Draw Underpriced at 13.5%
cards.summary: Sharp sportsbook consensus prices the draw at ~16-17% for this World Cup Group I match, while the market sits at just 13.5%, offering a roughly 2.5 percentage point edge on a low-probability outcome.
why: Leading sharp sportsbooks imply a 17% draw probability vs. the market's 13.5%
Both teams sit on 0 points entering the final group match, creating unpredictable desperation dynamics
The ~18% ROI on capital makes this a favorable risk/reward bet despite draws losing most of the time
cards.watch_item: Pre-kickoff line movement at sharp sportsbooks—if Pinnacle's draw odds drift down toward 13-14%, the edge disappears

cards.title: South Africa vs Korea Republic
cards.headline: South Africa vs Korea Republic: Market Prices Well-Calibrated, No Strong Edge
cards.summary: Korea Republic is priced at 60.5% to win their Women's World Cup Group A match against South Africa, which aligns closely with sportsbook consensus of 57-60%—leaving only a marginal 2-3 point edge on a sell.
why: Sportsbook consensus places Korea's win probability at 57-60%, slightly below Kalshi's 60.5% price
Korea only needs a draw to advance, potentially reducing their urgency to push for a win
All three contracts (Korea, Tie, South Africa) are within 1-3 points of fair value—no high-conviction opportunity
cards.watch_item: Late line movement at major sportsbooks before kickoff could confirm or widen the marginal edge on Korea's price

cards.title: Norway vs France
cards.headline: Norway vs France: Margins Too Thin to Trade
cards.summary: France is slightly underpriced as a ~57% favorite in this World Cup group-stage decider, but the edge over current market pricing is too slim to justify a confident position.
why: Sportsbook consensus implies France at 57-58% — Kalshi has them at 55.5%, a gap of only ~1.5 points
Both teams already qualified on 6 points, but group winner gets an easier Round of 32 path, keeping France motivated
All edges fall below the 3-point threshold typically needed for actionable trades in this market type
cards.watch_item: Lineup announcements — if either team rests key starters (especially Haaland or Mbappé), draw probability rises and France's edge could evaporate or widen significantly
